issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Milkable.messageOnMilk: The problem statement (and UML/examples) specify a no-argument method messageOnMilk() returning a String (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). The template's Main calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments. The solution repository instead declares the interface method as messageOnMilk(double volume) and all solution implementations (Seal, Goat) implement this double-parameter variant. This inconsistency prevents the template/example code from compiling against the solution API and confuses students which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the signature mismatch. Preferred fix (preserves the UML and template): change the solution to declare Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters returning String, and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). Update Milkable.java, Seal.java, and Goat.java accordingly. Alternative fix: update the problem statement, UML, and template (Main) to document and use messageOnMilk(double volume) consistently, including updating example calls and the described return format to include the volume. Prefer keeping the no-argument variant to match the UML and template usage.

issues.description: The milking method concept is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and UML declare a Milkable interface with a no-argument method messageOnMilk() returning a String and Part 2 explicitly states messageOnMilk() should return the phrase "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (problem_statement.md). The template Main.java also calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments. In the solution repository the Milkable interface is declared as messageOnMilk(double volume) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java) and the Seal and Goat classes implement messageOnMilk(double) and include the volume in the returned string (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java). This signature/identifier mismatch prevents a clear mapping from the exercise requirements to the reference implementation and will confuse or block students implementing the no-arg API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent. Preferred: change the solution to match the problem/template by declaring Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters and String return type, and update Seal and Goat to implement public String messageOnMilk() that returns exactly "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). Alternatively, if the volume parameter is intentionally required, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main.java to document and call messageOnMilk(double volume) and specify the expected output including the volume.
